title: Operator knowledge anchoring and oncall localization roadmap
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview
======
This roadmap describes a 12–18 month program to anchor operational knowledge, reduce cognitive load on platform operators, and localize oncall context (region / team / service) so SREs and platform operators can react more quickly and consistently to incidents. It focuses on three pillars: canonical runbooks and signatures, localized operator surfaces (dashboards & briefings), and knowledge anchoring mechanisms (training, certification, and durable artifacts).

Goals
-----
- Reduce mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for top 10 platform degradations by 25% within 12 months.
- Cut operator context-switch time (time to find relevant runbook + config) by 40%.
- Ensure each regional oncall rotation has a localized briefing bundle and validated runbook coverage for 95% of customer-facing services.
- Create verifiable knowledge anchors: certification pass rate >= 80% for primary oncall and 60% for secondary

Scope and exclusions
--------------------
Scope:
- Platform operator surfaces owned by eng-platform (prefetch, KV cache, routing, allocator, batcher, model-variant fallback).
- Runbook coverage for regionally deployed services and multi-tenant runtime components.
- Dashboards and alert subscriptions tied to localized operator bundles.

Exclusions:
- Customer-specific private deployment runbooks (moved to eng-private-deployments).
- Deep model internals (research-owned).

Principles
----------
1. Treat runbooks as executable artifacts: include required queries, console snippets, and expected outputs.
2. Localize before you generalize: create small localized bundles that reference canonical guides.
3. Measure knowledge surface area: track coverage, recency, and operator confidence as first-class metrics.
4. Automate verification: test runbooks with synthetic incidents in the lab.

High-level timeline (quarters)
----------------------------
| Quarter | Focus area | Deliverables | Success metric |
| Q4 2025 | Inventory & triage | Top-30 incident types mapped to owner + canonical runbook template | Mapping completed for 30 types |
| Q1 2026 | Runbook authoring & executable templates | 60% of top-30 runbooks converted to executable templates (CLI + dashboard links) | 60% coverage + automated smoke tests |
| Q2 2026 | Localization bundles & dashboards | Localized briefing bundles for 3 regions, dashboard templates, alert subscription presets | Bundles used on 2 live incidents |
| Q3 2026 | Training & certification pilot | Pilot certification for operator cohort (20 people) + gamified lab exercises | >= 75% pilot pass rate |
| Q4 2026 | Verification & scale | Synthetic incident sweep across all regions; 80% runbook verifications pass | MTTM decreased (pilot regions) |
| H1 2027 | Operationalize & embed | Integrate with new-hire path, onboarding, and release process for runbooks | Certification pass rate, coverage metrics in dashboards |

Workstreams and owners
----------------------
- Cataloging & metadata (owner: platform-telemetry team): inventory, tagging, freshness timestamps.
- Runbook engineering (owner: platform-ops): convert playbooks to executable templates, add CLI snippets and test harness.
- Dashboard localization (owner: platform-observability): per-region/tenant briefing bundles, alert presets, incident-summary cards.
- Training & certification (owner: platform-ops + people-ops): lab curriculum, assessment, recert cadence.
- Automation & verification (owner: platform-sre): synthetic incidents, smoke tests, continuous runbook verification.

Deliverable details
-------------------
1) Executable runbook template (example sections)
- Title, scope, related services
- Owner and escalation path
- Preconditions and safety checklist
- Detection queries (PromQL / SQL) and expected normal / degraded signatures
- Diagnosis steps (numbered): include CLI commands and sample outputs
- Mitigation steps (numbered): with rollback and verification commands
- Postmortem triggers and telemetry to record

2) Localized briefing bundle (example)
- One-page incident cheat sheet (service summary, recent deploys, capacity metrics snapshot)
- Dashboard URL + widget IDs
- Recommended subscriptions (pager, slack channel)
- Short list of 3 actions to try first, with command snippets

3) Certification & training kit
- 6-hour lab exercises covering: KV cache shard loss, mass-eviction, model-variant fallback, and regional routing split.
- Graded assessments with scenario-based rubrics.
- Re-certification policy: biannual for primary oncall, annual for secondary.

Example dashboard specification (table)
| Widget | Purpose | Query / Source | Visible to | Refresh |
| Operator briefing card | snapshot of top signals | TENANT_OVERVIEW(v1) | region-oncall | 15s |
| Runbook quicklink panel | jump to executable runbook | runbook://service/kv-cache/eviction | oncall + incident responders | static |
| Token surge heatmap | detect burst patterns | token.latency_heatmap() | platform-ops | 30s |

Rollout and verification procedure (numbered)
1. Inventory: create mapping (owner, severity, top signals) for top-30 incident types.
2. Author: convert 10 runbooks to executable templates; include smoke tests.
3. Localize: produce briefing bundles for pilot region (us-west-2).
4. Train: run 2 lab sessions with pilot operators; capture pass/fail and subjective confidence scores.
5. Verify: execute synthetic incident sweep for pilot region and measure MTTM and context-switch time.
6. Iterate: fix gaps and expand to remaining regions.

Metrics and dashboards to track
- Runbook coverage % (top-30)
- Runbook verification pass rate (automated smoke tests)
- Operator certification pass rate
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for top-10 incidents
- Context switch time (time from alert to first mitigation command executed)
- Operator satisfaction (quarterly NPS)

Risks and mitigations
---------------------
- Risk: Runbook rot due to changes in service contracts.
  Mitigation: runbook freshness tags + break-the-build guard that fails release if critical signals schema changes without runbook update.
- Risk: Overlocalization creates divergence across regions.
  Mitigation: ensure canonical runbook exists and local bundles only add context, not contradict mitigation steps.
- Risk: Training is ignored due to operational load.
  Mitigation: require certification for primary oncall and enforce shadowing windows for new hires.

Budget and resourcing ask (summary)
- 0.6 FTE platform-telemetry (6 months) for metadata and cataloging.
- 1.2 FTE runbook engineering (9 months) to convert templates + test harness.
- 0.4 FTE platform-observability (6 months) for dashboard templates and automation.
- Lab credit: small synthetic incident run budget (~$12k) for traffic replay and test harness.

Adoption checklist (pre-launch)
- [ ] Top-30 incident mapping completed and owners assigned
- [ ] 10 executable runbooks authored and smoke-tested
- [ ] Pilot region briefing bundles created and validated
- [ ] First training cohort scheduled and materials created
- [ ] Monitoring dashboard for coverage and verification live

Appendices
---------
A. Runbook template example (CLI snippet)
- kubectl -n platform logs -l app=kv-cache | grep eviction | tail -n 200
- curl -sS "https://ops-api.internal/v1/evictions?region=us-west-2" | jq '.summary'

B. Synthetic incident test plan (short)
1. Seed KV cache with 10M prefixes; induce time-correlated evictions on a subset of shards.
2. Verify operator runbook leads to eviction containment and client recovery within 12 minutes.
3. Record telemetry for post-runbook tuning.

C. Governance: runbook review cadence
- Owners must review and sign off runbooks every 90 days; automated reminder emails generated by cataloging service.

Next steps (immediate)
---------------------
1. Approve the resourcing ask and kick off the inventory sprint (two-week cadence).
2. Assign pilot region owner and schedule first lab in Q1 2026.
3. Add the verification dashboard to the operator home page and link the pilot bundles.
